title: Small products of dg model categories and enriched localizations
statement:
Use cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and enriched localization as in [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]. Fix universes large enough for all the categories and small families below. A combinatorial differential graded model category is a complete and cocomplete locally presentable category enriched, tensored and cotensored over unbounded complexes of abelian groups, with retract-closed classes of cofibrations, fibrations and weak equivalences; weak equivalences satisfy two-out-of-three, and (cofibrations, trivial fibrations) and (trivial cofibrations, fibrations) are functorial weak factorization systems generated by sets. Trivial means also a weak equivalence. A weak factorization system has factorizations and two classes characterized by their mutual diagonal-lifting properties. Locally presentable means cocomplete and generated under sufficiently filtered colimits by a small set of presentable objects, where an object is presentable if its Hom functor preserves those filtered colimits. Require the enriched model axiom: the Hom-complex map associated to a cofibration and a fibration is a degreewise surjection, and a quasi-isomorphism if either map is trivial.

Let $J$ be any small set, possibly empty, and let $(\mathcal M_j)_{j\in J}$ be such categories with weak equivalences $W_j$. The product $\mathcal P=\prod_{j\in J}\mathcal M_j$ has a combinatorial differential graded model structure whose three model classes are detected coordinatewise, whose Hom complexes are products, and whose tensors and cotensors are coordinatewise. Cofibrant, fibrant and bifibrant objects are exactly the respective coordinatewise objects. With $W_{\mathcal P}$ the coordinatewise weak equivalences, the evaluation comparison is an equivalence of enhanced categories
$$\mathcal P[W_{\mathcal P}^{-1}]\simeq\prod_{j\in J}\mathcal M_j[W_j^{-1}],$$
with natural mapping-object identification
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(X,Y)\simeq\prod_{j\in J}^{\mathbf R}R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M_j}(X_j,Y_j).$$
For cofibrant $X$ and fibrant $Y$, the ordinary product complex $\prod_j\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X_j,Y_j)$ represents this derived product. These identifications preserve evaluations, composition, identities, and all their coherent homotopies.
